item.title: Rhode Island Sues Meta Over Alleged Tolerance for Scam Advertising
item.description: Rhode Island sued Meta Platforms in state court last week over the company’s alleged tolerance for widespread scam advertising on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms. The suit, filed by Rhode Island Attorney General Peter Neronha in Providence Superior Court, accuses Meta of unlawfully profiting from and participating in the creation of billions of dollars in scam advertising – even as it assured its billions of users that it was working diligently to protect them. Related: Meta to Pay Historic $25 Billion in New Mexico Deception Case The complaint seeks monetary civil penalties for each of Meta’s alleged violations of Rhode Island state law, restitution to consumers, disgorgement of ill-gotten gains and a judicial order requiring the company to address, rather than profit from, scam ads it develops and delivers on its platforms.

item.title: FEMA Launches Online Purchasing for Flood Insurance Policies
item.description: Related: National Flood Insurance Program’s Authority to Expire in December Flood damage is not covered by standard homeowners and renters insurance policies. The Federal Emergency Management Agency said it has launched a new tool for residents to buy flood insurance through the National Flood Insurance Program. “With this new digital tool, you can get a quote and buy a flood insurance policy in a matter of minutes.” Homeowners can get a free quote after entering information such as address, foundation type, construction type, elevation, and location of HVAC systems.

item.title: Fast-Fashion Group Shein Paying $100 Million to Settle FTC Probe

Consumers filed more than 12,000 complaints about Shein over more than $11 million in purchases between January 2020 and June 2026, according to FTC records reviewed by Reuters.

item.title: When Traction Becomes Personal Exposure: What The Joonko Guilty Plea Means For Founders

The distinction between future potential and present-day facts matters when describing customers, revenue and traction. item.title: VKB returns seeking lower-attaching renewal of King Max Re German multi-peril cat bond
item.description: Versicherungskammer Bayern Versicherungsanstalt des oeffentlichen Rechts’ (VKB), the German domestic market insurance group, is back in the catastrophe bond market looking to renew coverage from its soon to mature debut deal, by sponsoring a currently €150 million King Max Re II DAC (Series 2026-1) German multi-peril transaction, we have learned. VKB sponsored its debut cat bond in late 2023, securing an upsized €175 million of multi-peril catastrophe reinsurance protection from the King Max Re DAC 2023 issuance, which became one of only a handful of catastrophe bond transactions ever to solely have a focus on transferring German perils to the capital markets. That cat bond sponsored in 2023 is scheduled to mature in early January 2027, hence this new offering that has come to light appears to be a renewal of the multi-peril reinsurance coverage for the sponsor.

Then, in our second update on the cat bond offering, the target size was further increased, with $450 million of parametric earthquake reinsurance limit being sought and at the same time the price guidance was reduced again.

item.title: Liberty Mutual Re and Celest.Science explore parametric trigger data fallback
item.description: Liberty Mutual Reinsurance (LM Re) part of Liberty Mutual Insurance Group, and Celest.Science have announced a collaboration to explore the development of a potential fallback methodology intended to support event characterisation for parametric tropical cyclone insurance when crucial weather data is either unavailable or delayed. As per the announcement, the collaboration between the two companies will explore how LM Re’s parametric risk transfer expertise and Celest.Science’s climate modelling capabilities can be combined to develop and test a potential missing data methodology. Our collaboration with Celest.Science enables us to explore options that could provide that extra layer of resilience, even if a primary data source becomes unavailable.”

item.title: Fla. Reforms Cut Property Premiums but Data Show Multifamily Liability Rates Up
item.description: Data from Advocate Technologies, a data analytics firm that tracks commercial and commercial residential rates around the country for the insurance industry, show that property insurance premiums for multifamily dwellings in Florida, like those for most other properties, have indeed fallen sharply in the last two years. In other words, it seems that Florida’s historic 2022 and 2023 legislative reforms have had a significant impact on property insurance by disincentivizing excessive claims litigation, but liability claims and lawsuits continue to cost insurers and insureds, at least in the multifamily segment, the Advocate data and reports suggest. The data for more than 1,000 Florida properties show that for Florida multifamily property insurance for all categories of structures and coverage, except condominiums, with primary and excess coverage included, the median premium per door has dropped from an early 2025 number of $797—almost double the rate in other Southeastern states—to $472 in April of this year.

item.title: Transit Systems Weigh Whether to Run Trains Without a Human at the Controls
item.description: The Washington and LA projects, which would take years to implement and still face financial and technical hurdles, come amid an already fierce debate over the safety risks and benefits of automated trains and whether the substantial upfront expense is worth the long-term savings in labor costs. It’ll stretch 19 miles when completed, surpassing the elevated driverless trains Detroit and Miami opened as pilot projects in the 1980s, a monorail connecting hotels on the Las Vegas Strip, and smaller systems that carry passengers between airport terminals. Even as automated vehicles such as robotaxis grow more prevalent in the U.S., almost every mass transit system still requires a driver or operator on board.

item.title: Hacking Attempts Surge as Companies, Governments Rush to Patch PHP Flaws
item.description: Global firms and governments rushed on Thursday to patch critical flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet, as cloud firms reported a surge of hacking attempts after the vulnerabilities were disclosed. As companies and governments deployed patches and suspended websites as a precaution, hacking attempts surged into the millions, according to cloud services firm Cloudflare and Amazon. The emergency shutdowns of banking, airline, rail, tax and government services from Tokyo to Helsinki mark one of the most dramatic tests of the decades-old programming tools that keep the web running, exposing how deeply governments and companies depend on code that few people understand.

item.title: Animals Cause More Than 350,000 Crashes Per Year: Report
item.description: Roadway crashes involving animals account for a significant number of crashes each year, according to a new report by the AAA Foundation for Traffic Safety. More than 350,000 crashes, nearly 50,000 injuries, and nearly 300 deaths each year occur when a motorist strikes or attempts to avoid an animal, the authors Ansley Kasha, Lin-Kuei Huang, and principal researcher Brian C. The majority of animal-related crashes that lead to death involved other events more severe than striking the animal, such as striking a tree, colliding with another vehicle, or rolling over, which suggests that taking sudden evasive action to attempt to avoid striking an animal may be riskier than striking it.

item.title: USAA secures 56% upsized $350m Residential Re 2026-2 cat bond priced below guidance
item.description: USAA has now priced and secured the 56% upsized target of $350 million of multi-year per-occurrence reinsurance coverage from its new Residential Reinsurance 2026 Limited (Series 2026-2) catastrophe bond issuance, getting the capital markets coverage at pricing levels below guidance, Artemis can report. Now, we can report that USAA successfully finalised its latest cat bond sponsorship to provide the 56% upsized $350 million of multi-year per-occurrence reinsurance protection, while the pricing was finalised at a below initial guidance level for all three tranches of notes. Once settled, all three tranches of Residential Reinsurance 2026-2 cat bond notes will provide USAA with four years of multi-peril per-occurrence catastrophe reinsurance protection on an indemnity trigger basis, running from December 1st, 2026, through to November 30th, 2030.

item.title: Michigan, Ohio Gas Prices Spike Further Amid Refinery Breakdown
item.description: Gas prices in two Midwestern battleground states saw further hikes on Thursday as the region’s market grapples with a refinery issue in Illinois. In Michigan, prices rose to $4.74 a gallon on Thursday, up from $4.59 a gallon on Wednesday, according to GasBuddy , a fuel savings app that tracks prices in live time. In Ohio, prices stood at $4.34 a gallon, up from $4.05 a gallon on Wednesday.

item.title: Oklahoma Landlord to Pay $52K for Violating Fair Housing Act
item.description: The Justice Department announced that the owners of a residential rental property in Oklahoma City have agreed to pay $52,500 to resolve a lawsuit alleging that they refused to rent a one-bedroom apartment to a single mother upon learning that she would be living with her child, in violation of the Fair Housing Act. The Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in housing against families with children. District Court for the Western District of Oklahoma in August 2025, alleges that in July 2022 a woman inquired about renting a one-bedroom unit in Defendants’ 36-unit apartment complex known as The Vintage at Mesta Park.

item.title: DoorDash launches restaurant insurance with Authentic

item.title: Storm Austen Knocks Out Power to Nearly 300,000 French Homes
item.description: Austen is the first named storm this autumn and it’s also sending power prices in France and Germany tumbling. Storm Austen knocked out electricity to almost 300,000 customers in western France on Friday as hurricane-force winds battered the region, disrupting roads, railways and other transport links. Brittany was hardest hit, with almost 150,000 customers without power, according to distributor Enedis.

item.title: Insurance AI’s Next Test: Can Carriers Trust the Data?
item.description: Insurance companies are beginning to look toward the next phase of AI adoption with agentic AI and automation, according to Chris Newman, CEO of ACORD Solutions Group, at this year’s InsurTech Connect conference in Las Vegas. However, as AI moves further into insurance decision-making and business operations, insurers need confidence in the data supporting the technology. “But the challenge comes with the trust element in terms of can you trust your data.” This means questions of where the information originated, whether sources are verified, and if a carrier can account for how decisions are made, he said.

item.title: U.S. Announces $25M Whistleblower Program to Encourage Public to Report Alleged Fraud
item.description: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday announced a $25 million program to encourage the public to blow the whistle on suspected fraud in the U.S. The White House said that under the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program, anyone who submits a tip that leads to a fraud conviction or a significant federal enforcement action is eligible to receive up to $30,000, and that the Justice Department will administer the program. During the announcement, Trump said payments will amount to a 1% commission on the amount of fraud the tip helps uncover.

item.title: China’s Natural Disaster Losses Hit $30B in First Nine Months of 2026
item.description: China recorded 199.36 billion yuan ($29.9 billion) in direct losses from natural disasters in the first nine months of 2026, mainly driven by severe typhoons, flooding and landslides, its Ministry of Emergency Management said on Thursday. Overall, 1,162 people have died or have been classified as missing from China’s natural disasters in the first nine months of the year, up from 742 a year earlier. The losses were down 8% from 217.65 billion yuan over the same period last year.

item.title: Fronting companies to engage more frequently with ILS market: AM Best
item.description: Rating agency AM Best has indicated in a new report that fronting companies are expected to engage more frequently with the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market to drive capacity diversification using catastrophe bonds, sidecars and collateralized reinsurance structures. item.title: Munich Re raises full-year 2026 profit target as Q3 result well-above consensus
item.description: As a result, with this above the previous target that was expected, Munich Re has now raised its full-year 2026 profit target by €300 million, from €6.3 billion to €6.6 billion. Demonstrating the continued profitability of reinsurance underwriting businesses in 2026, global giant Munich Re has preliminarily reported its third-quarter net profit will be higher than consensus at €1.7 billion, on which basis the company has raised its full-year profit guidance by €300 million. Munich Re said today that the third-quarter of 2026 saw strong financial performance for the company, resulting in a net profit projected to be €1.7 billion, much higher than the analyst consensus estimate of €1.479 billion.
